<reason>Side A wins on the burden-flip: sustaining a veto needs only a minority while ending powers without sunsets can require overriding it, leaving executives protected by inertia. B's tailored, appropriations, and parliamentary alternatives were damaged by A's conditional-renewal leverage and the point that bans, censorship, and regulatory suspensions need no funding to defund. B's cliff and rubber-stamp dilemma remained forceful, but A answered it with time-sensitive, clause-by-clause renewal.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was A's closing answer to B's appropriations alternative: defunding cannot repeal zero-cost coercive decrees, while repeal or amendment remains blocked by veto or party loyalty.</best_rebuttal>
